questions.question: Why should AI architecture decisions be recorded?
options: Because tradeoffs should be hidden from future teams who inherit the decision
Because reversibility never matters once an architecture decision has shipped
Because an ADR record replaces the need for a separate security review and approval entirely
Because model, vendor, security, and cost choices can become expensive defaults
questions.explanation: Recorded decisions preserve context so model, vendor, security, and cost choices don't quietly become expensive defaults — tradeoffs shouldn't be hidden, reversibility still matters, and an ADR doesn't substitute for security review.

questions.question: A team adopts a proprietary vector database with a data format and query API that no other vendor supports, without ever discussing what switching away would cost later. Which of the lesson's four signals does this match most directly?
options: Vendor lock-in — the chosen technology makes switching to an alternative costly or difficult later
Technical uncertainty — the team isn't sure the chosen approach will even work at the required scale
Security boundary — the decision changes who or what can access sensitive data
Cost tradeoff — the decision trades a lower price today for a higher price later
questions.explanation: Choosing a proprietary format with no viable exit path is the lesson's vendor-lock-in signal — distinct from technical uncertainty (unproven feasibility), a security boundary change, or a cost tradeoff.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A finished, deployable production system ready to serve live traffic
An itemized cloud invoice showing the cost of each architecture option, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
A ranked architecture decision plan with governance controls for each option
A user survey measuring satisfaction with the chosen architecture
questions.explanation: The artifact ranks scenarios into an architecture decision plan with governance controls, recommending a design note, ADR, or review path — it doesn't build a production system, generate an invoice, or run a survey.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: Ignoring the cost model because the architecture decision needs to ship quickly
Skipping the review board because the team is confident in its own judgment
Threat model — a review of who could misuse the new architecture and how
Hiding the alternatives that were considered so the ADR looks more decisive
questions.explanation: The lesson's controls are ADR record, threat model, cost model, and review board — a threat model reviews who could misuse the architecture, unlike ignoring cost, skipping review, or hiding alternatives.

questions.question: When does an AI architecture decision need stronger governance?
options: Only when there is no security boundary involved in the decision at all
Only when the architecture choice is trivial and easy to reverse later
When impact is high, reversibility is low, or security, vendor, or cost tradeoffs exist
Never — documenting implementation details is enough governance on its own — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
questions.explanation: High impact, low reversibility, or security, vendor, or cost tradeoffs are exactly when governance should strengthen — not the absence of a security boundary, a trivial choice, or implementation notes alone.

questions.question: What should an AI architecture decision record include?
options: The decision, alternatives considered, consequences, threat model, and cost tradeoff
Only the name of the vendor that was ultimately chosen for the project
No alternatives, since listing rejected options makes the record longer, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
No trigger for revisiting the decision later, once it has been approved
questions.explanation: An ADR should record the decision, the alternatives considered, consequences, the threat model, and the cost tradeoff — not just a vendor name, a record with no alternatives, or one with no revisit trigger.
